t: Chamath Palihapitiya on venture capital as a Ponzi scheme
ot: Venture Capital - Silicon Valley Ponzi Scheme - Chamath Palihapitiya
why: Linked when people argue that venture valuations are set by the next round of investors rather than by the business.

mentions.x: This is relevant: [video] Silicon valley Ponzi scheme
…then they just need to show/push fast initial growth to attract more layers of investment and it doesn't necessarily need to make long term sense. Chamath Palihapitiya describes this here: [video]
VCs also get paid by getting other VCs to evaluate their companies as more valuable in a sort of Ponzi scheme: [video]
…(coming from Chamath Palihapitiya; a billionaire who was one of the first Facebook employees): [video] And let's not ignore that the entire financial system within which this ponzi scheme…
…shouldn’t have been funded in the first place. They create a market that artificially props up unsustainable businesses. This video is a good explanation of how the VC world actually works. [video]
…Palihapitiya talked about this in 2019, and others before then although I don't have references. [video] Warning, video is self-serving but simplistically, this is part of it. To be clear, the VCs…
VCs do like to stack their imaginary value stores like Russian dolls [video]
